# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 15 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 15
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. And about the Sabbath — here is what is written in the Ten Commandments that God spoke directly to Moses on Mount Sinai: "Keep the Sabbath of the Lord holy, with clean hands and a pure heart."
2. And in another place: "If my sons observe the Sabbath, I will show them my mercy."
3. At the very beginning of creation, the Sabbath appears: "God completed the works of his hands in six days. On the seventh day he finished, rested, and made it holy."
4. Pay attention, children — what does "he completed everything in six days" mean? It means this: in six thousand years the Lord will bring everything to its end. A day with him equals a thousand years, and he himself testifies to this: "Look — the day of the Lord is as a thousand years." So, children: six days = six thousand years, and that is when everything will be finished.
5. "And he rested on the seventh day." This means: when the Son comes, he will end the era of the Lawless One, judge the ungodly, and transform the sun, moon, and stars — and then he will truly rest on the seventh day.
6. He also says: "Hallow it with clean hands and a pure heart." If anyone today is actually capable of making holy the day that God made holy — while being pure in heart — then we are entirely deceived.
7. Here is the truth: we will truly rest and make it holy at that future time — when we have been made righteous, when we have received the promise, when lawlessness is over and the Lord has made everything new. Only then will we be able to make it holy — because only then will we ourselves be holy.
8. He says to them: "Your new moons and your sabbaths — I cannot stand them." Do you see what he means? The sabbaths you keep now are not acceptable to me. The one I made is the one that matters — when I have brought all things to rest, I will begin the eighth day: the start of another world entirely.
9. And that is why we celebrate the eighth day with joy — the day Jesus rose from the dead, and from which, after appearing, he ascended into the heavens.
